screens.title: The method
screens.prose:
Every follow-up here went the same way. Solve the general case, check it on the case you solved, then substitute:

$$E[\max] = \frac{(n + 1)(4n - 1)}{6n}, \qquad V = E[\max(X, V - c)], \qquad x = \frac{p}{1 - (1 - p)^k}.$$

screens.title: Derive the larger of two
screens.prose: Derive the mean of the larger of two $n$-sided dice, one justified line at a time.

The larger of two uniforms on $[0, n]$ averages $\tfrac{2n}{3}$, so $E[\max] = \tfrac{2n}{3}$.

screens.title: Write it
screens.prose: Write `max_of_two(n)` and `reroll_value(faces, cost)`, both returning a `Fraction`. For the reroll game, try every rule "keep faces of at least $t$". Its value solves $V = \tfrac{\text{kept faces} + (t - 1)(V - c)}{n}$; return the best.
screens.question: Write both functions.

widget.starter:
from fractions import Fraction


def max_of_two(n):
    """Mean of the larger of two fair n-sided dice."""
    ...


def reroll_value(faces, cost):
    """Value of: keep the face, or pay cost to reroll, as often as you like."""
    ...
widget.solution:
from fractions import Fraction


def max_of_two(n):
    """Mean of the larger of two fair n-sided dice."""
    return Fraction((n + 1) * (4 * n - 1), 6 * n)


def reroll_value(faces, cost):
    """Value of: keep the face, or pay cost to reroll, as often as you like."""
    cost = Fraction(cost)
    best = None
    for t in range(1, faces + 1):      # keep faces t and above
        rerolled = t - 1
        kept = sum(range(t, faces + 1))
        v = (kept - rerolled * cost) / (faces - rerolled)
        if best is None or v > best:
            best = v
    return best

That gives $V = \tfrac{\text{kept} - (t - 1)c}{n - t + 1}$; take the largest over $t$.

byKey.test-5: At cost £1 the best rule keeps 3 or more, worth £4.

explain.text: Each threshold rule gives one linear equation in $V$, and the best rule gives the value. A 10-sided die at £1 keeps 6 or more, worth £7. A 20-sided die keeps 15 or more, worth $\tfrac{91}{6} \approx \text{£}15.17$.

screens.title: Follow-up: the third question
screens.prose: The interviewer's third question on the reroll game: an $n$-sided die, and a cost $c$ a reroll. State the rule in one sentence.
screens.question: Which rule is right?

options.text: Keep any face of at least $V - c$, where $V$ solves $V = E[\max(X, V - c)]$
Keep any face above the mean, $\tfrac{n + 1}{2}$
options.why: That ignores the cost. At $c = 0$ you would reroll until $n$.

options.text: Reroll whenever one more roll gains more than $c$ on average
options.why: That looks one roll ahead. You may reroll again, so compare with $V - c$, not with one roll.

options.text: Keep any face of at least $n - c$
options.why: That fails at $n = 6$, $c = 1$: it says keep 5 or more, but the best rule keeps 3 or more.

hints.text: What do you get if you reroll?
A reroll costs $c$ and puts you back at the start, worth $V$.
So keep $x$ exactly when $x \ge V - c$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare a face with what rerolling is worth.

byKey.c: You looked one roll ahead. The option to reroll again is part of what a reroll is worth.

explain.text: Rerolling costs $c$ and restarts a game worth $V$, so a face $x$ is kept when $x \ge V - c$. At $n = 6$, $c = 1$, that is $V - c = 3$: keep 3 or more, as in l1.

screens.title: The minute after
screens.prose: A market-making interviewer has your price for the larger of two dice, $\tfrac{161}{36}$. Now they want a fair price for a bet paying the larger of two 100-sided dice, in £.
screens.question: What is the fair price? Give three decimal places.

hints.text: You already have the general case.
Check $\tfrac{(n + 1)(4n - 1)}{6n}$ at $n = 6$ first.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Substitute $n = 100$ into the checked formula.

byKey.continuous: That is $\tfrac{2n}{3}$, the continuous limit. It is close, but the bet pays whole faces.
byKey.mean: That is the mean of one die. The larger of two sits higher.

explain.text: Stating the general case first turned the follow-up into one substitution: $\tfrac{40299}{600} = \text{£}67.165$. The continuous shortcut gives £66.67, off by half a pound on a tight market. The check at $n = 6$ takes seconds and protects the quote.

ideas: Interviewers extend a solved puzzle at once, so solve the general case.
Check the general answer on the case you solved, and on $n = 1$, before you substitute.
A cost per reroll keeps the threshold rule: keep $x$ when $x \ge V - c$.
summary.trap: Trusting a general formula you have not tested on the case you already solved.
